A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same FiSeR research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F. Text and rendered-page comparisons identify differences only on pages 1 and 7; all appendices are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-detection experiments, few-shot adaptation, ablations, robustness tests, representation analyses, and Monte Carlo simulations in Section 4 and Appendices C-F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and simulation results, with limited numerical corrections in the main text.

M1.justification: The hierarchical coarse/fine contrastive objectives, encoder training, and frozen-backbone inference with lightweight classification heads are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WildFake, Community Forensics, AIGIBench, Chameleon, and GenImage coverage, including the same corruption scenarios and Monte Carlo geometries.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the experiments. Tables 1 and 4 revise scores for existing comparators without adding, removing, or modifying comparison methods.

E3.justification: Training settings, source/target assignments, metrics, backbone configurations, and few-shot procedures are unchanged. The numerical corrections do not document a protocol change or establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same loss and backbone ablations, classification-head comparison, shot-count analyses, perturbation tests, and representation analyses remain. Table 4 corrects an existing result without adding or redesigning an analysis.

E5.justification: Few-shot results still use mean±std over five random draws, and the Monte Carlo sampling procedure is unchanged. Table 4's revised standard-deviation value changes a result, not the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes ResNet50-Detection's direct Chameleon AUROC from 56.04 to 63.65, reducing its SVM gain from +36.34 to +28.73 while retaining 92.38 after adaptation; Section 4.3 follows this correction. Table 4 changes CLIPDetection's AIGIBench SVM result from 78.86±1.63 to 86.97±2.39 and the SVM average from 86.47 to 87.82. SVM consequently replaces Linear as CLIPDetection's best reported head. These limited corrections agree with results already present in Appendix F.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Section 3, homophily normalization, and random-mixing proposition and proof in Appendix B are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about transferable representations, hierarchical contrastive learning, homophily, and lightweight adaptation. Their headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning classifier-boundary mismatch, representation transferability, classifier independence, and robustness are unchanged. Section 4.3 updates a supporting number without changing its explanation; the impact qualifications also remain identical.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing information, and classifier implementations. Code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to previous detectors are unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Apart from the corrected numerical statement in Section 4.3, wording, terminology, section organization, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 moves the CLIPDetection row's boldface emphasis from Linear to SVM to reflect the corrected ranking. Figures, captions, table structures, placement, and overall layout otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves identifiable reporting inconsistencies. Table 1 now agrees with ResNet-50's result in Tables 2 and 8 and no longer overstates its adaptation gain. Table 4 now uses the WildFake-trained CLIPDetection result from Table 8 instead of the Community-trained value appearing in Table 9, with the average updated accordingly. These corrections improve internal consistency and comparison accuracy while leaving the method, experimental scope, and main conclusions unchanged.
